sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 and height 5.

steps: Identify the quantities and the applicable model.
Check that the result answers the question.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: Find the exact volume of a cone with radius 4 units and height 21 units. Express your answer as a rational multiple of π.
Find the exact volume of a sphere with radius 9 units. Express your answer as a rational multiple of π.
A cylinder and cone each have radius 3 units and height 3 units. Which has the greater volume?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: As x increases, y generally decreases. What association does this scatter plot describe?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Most plotted points follow y = 2x + 1. Of these points, (6, 13), (7, 15), (5, 11), (6, 28), which point is an outlier?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A line of fit is y = 2x + 5. Predict y when x = 3.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
